newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases as oil firms seek dollars.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases as oil firms seek dollars.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased marginally on Tuesday on strong demand for hard currencies from the oil industry, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.94 against the dollar compared to 53.91 on Monday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 87.58 from 87.29.
Dealers said the interbank market was active with good interest from both sides -- keeping it locked within the 53.80/54.05 range.
"With coffee and tea dollars coming in today, we shall see if the shilling will break the 54 level," one dealer said.
The money market was tight with overnight rates quoted unchanged around the 23 percent levels.
